deep.reconstruction:
Context: Göttingen, 30 April 1832. This is part of the work that became 'Intensitas vis magneticae terrestris ad mensuram absolutam revocata'. Needle A is a magnetometer needle read with a theodolite, mirror and scale. One scale division is 26.868"; the theodolite stays at 224°3'30".

(I) Loaded oscillations, second load position. The previous page has needle A loaded with two 100 g weights at mutual distance 229.25 mm, giving period t1 = 26.4045 s. Here the same weights are at mutual distance 39.025 mm. Each transit time T_n of oscillation n is reduced to epoch 0 with a trial period of 21.16 s: R_n = T_n - 21.16 n. For example, 23h33'12.15" - 21.16 s = 23h32'50.99". For n = 32, 677.12 s = 11'17.12" is subtracted. For n = 79-81 the clock has passed midnight, so 24h is added.
- Group means: n = 2: 50.963 (written 50.96); n = 33: 51.103 (written 51.10); n = 80: 51.173 (written 51.17).
- Period: t2 = 21.16 + (51.173 - 50.963)/78 = 21.1627 s. Gauss uses the two end groups only; the middle group is a check. A least-squares line through all three groups gives 21.16259 s instead.
- NB: the unloaded period on 29 April was 20.9751 s.

(II) 'Stat. Mom. der Nadel'. Model: t^2 · MT = π^2 (K + Σ m r^2). Two loadings with the same weights give an expression in which the needle's own moment of inertia K and the weights' own moments cancel: MT/π^2 = ΔI/(t1^2 - t2^2), with ΔI = 2·m·[(d1/2)^2 - (d2/2)^2] = 50 (d1^2 - d2^2) in g·mm² for m = 100 g.
- Here ΔI = 50 (229.25^2 - 39.025^2) = 2 551 631 g·mm².
- t1^2 - t2^2 = 697.1976 - 447.8599 = 249.3378.
- Ratio: 10 233.6.
- If the chronometer runs on sidereal seconds and is reduced to mean time (factor 0.99727^2), the ratio becomes about 10 290.
- Gauss writes 10294, with log 4.01260 = log10(10294).
- My reading: the quantity is MT/π^2 (or MT in units absorbing π^2), in g, mm, mean-time s. The remaining discrepancy of about 0.04% (rate, exact weights, or torsion) is not reconstructable. This interpretation is mine and uncertain.

(III) Needle A after re-magnetising bars A and B on the great magnet. New oscillation series, trial period 17.426 s: R_n = T_n - 17.426 n, measured from 2h45'. For example, n = 119: 2079.3 - 2073.694 = 5.606. Group means (my check):
- n = 1-3: 5.348
- n = 119-122: 22.568/4 = 5.642
- n = 233-236: 5.503
- n = 338-342: 25.150/5 = 5.030
- n = 708-711: 21.612/4 = 5.403
The 'Mittelwerth' 17.42608 equals 17.426 + (5.403 - 5.348)/707.5 = 17.426078 s, again first and last groups only. A least-squares line through all five groups would give about 17.42583 s. The group means wander by ±0.3 s, so the period was not constant (temperature or rest-point drift).

(IV) Error estimate. Take residuals of each single reduced time from its group mean. The sum of squares is 0.012152 over 20 observations in 5 groups, so 15 degrees of freedom (my reconstruction). Then the mean error is sqrt(0.012152/15) = 0.02846 → 'Error medius 0"0285'. The probable error is 0.6745 × 0.0285 = 0.0192 → 'Error verisimilis 0"019'. 'Genauer berechnet … E.m. eines Antritts 0"0465' is a refined mean error of a single transit (Antritt). 0.0465/0.0285 ≈ 1.63 ≈ sqrt(8/3), possibly reflecting how each tabulated time is built from several scale transits. Not reconstructed.

(V) Logarithmic decrement. The table gives n, the rest point (drifting 263.8 → 275.4) and the arc (336.3 → 43.6). The decrement per oscillation is λ = log10(A_a/A_b)/(n_b - n_a), using pair means:
- 335.65 → 248.35 over 117 oscillations: 0.001118 → 0.00112
- 248.35 → 180.65 over 114: 0.001212 → 0.00121
- 180.65 → 134.2 over 106: 0.001218 → 0.00122
- 134.2 → 43.6 over 368.5: 0.001325 → 0.00132
- overall 335.65 → 43.6 over 705.5: 0.001256 → 0.00126
The decrement grows slightly as the arc shrinks. These data feed the arc (amplitude) correction to the period, which is applied on the next page ('Corr.').
errors: Group n = 708-711: with the raw times as read, 708 (6h10'42.0") gives 12342 - 708×17.426 = 4.392, not 5.392. Likewise 709 gives 4.366 and 711 gives 4.414. Only 710 (11'17.9") reproduces the written 5.440.

The raw intervals 708→709→710→711 as read are 17.4, 18.5, 16.4 s, which is implausible. Raw 710 should probably be 16.9", in which case all four reduced values should be 4.xxx, and Gauss's 5.392/5.366/5.440/5.414 carry a uniform +1 s reduction slip.

If that slip is real, the last group mean is 4.403 and the endpoint period becomes 17.426 + (4.403 - 5.348)/707.5 = 17.42466 s instead of 17.42608 s. The alternative is a misreading of the raw seconds; this cannot be settled from the image.

'Mittelwerth' 17.42608 (and 21.1627) uses only the first and last groups, not a least-squares fit over all groups (17.42583 and 21.16259 respectively). This is not an error, but the middle groups deviate by ±0.3 s, so the stated small error figures do not reflect the uncertainty of the period.

'Stat. Mom.' 10294: my reconstruction gives MT/π^2 ≈ 10234 g·mm²/s² in clock seconds, or ≈ 10290 if the clock is sidereal and reduced to mean time. This is close to 10294 but not exact; the remaining factor is unexplained.

results.what: Reduction of transit times with a trial period, then period from first and last group means
results.modern_name: Method of coincident epochs / linear drift fit of oscillation transit times
results.usually_credited_to: Standard pendulum/astronomical timing practice (Borda, Kater, Bessel)

results.what: Directive moment from two loadings with equal weights at different distances, eliminating the unknown moment of inertia
results.modern_name: Gauss's method of absolute moment-of-inertia determination (added masses)

results.what: Logarithmic decrement per oscillation from successive amplitudes, used for the arc correction
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Gauss and Weber used it in magnetometry)

results.what: Mean error from residuals about group means with (N - number of groups) degrees of freedom, and probable error = 0.6745 × mean error
results.modern_name: Unbiased residual standard deviation and probable error

deep.surprise_reason: Routine laboratory computation from Gauss's 1832 absolute-intensity experiments. All methods (loaded-oscillation method, logarithmic decrement, mean and probable error with degrees-of-freedom correction) are well known as his. Interest is archival only, including a probable 1-second reduction slip in the last group.

transcription_corrections: '[-10?94-] 10794' should read 10294 (bold digit written over); log 4.01260 = log10(10294).
'redu. a. 21"16' is 'reducirt auf 21"16' (reduced with trial period 21.16 s); likewise '17.426' heads the second reduction column.

Raw time for n = 710 ('11 17.9') is doubtful: intervals suggest 16.9, or else the raw times for 708, 709 and 711 are 1 s higher than read. The reduced 5.392-5.414 are inconsistent with the raw times as transcribed.
0.00126, written to the right, is the overall decrement from n ≈ 7.5 to 713, not a fifth interval value.
Middle columns of the amplitude table are the rest point (Nullpunkt) and the arc (Schwingung) in scale divisions, as on the previous page.
